description:
Generate several candidate designs for ONE brief so the user can pick.

A design usually starts here: the user describes what they want and gets
three options back. For a single design, or to refine one they already
picked, use `design_start_for_order`.

`prompt` MUST be the user's own description of the piece. Never synthesise a
brief, and never treat their choice of the design route as a description of
the artwork: if they have not said what they want, ask before calling this.
Each call spends `count` real generations, so a guessed brief wastes them all
and shows the user designs for something they never asked for.

Pass the order_id and the design brief; it provisions `count` designs
(default 3) against the order's
real geometry, generates each in parallel, and returns them as `candidates`
— each with a `design_id`, a short `summary`, a `design_url`, and
`thumbnails`. Pass `item_id` to design one item; it is required when the
order has several items (`OrderItemRequiredError` lists them). Each item
keeps its own design, so the items of an order can be designed side by side.
On an order with several items, an item whose design is already attached
fails with `DesignAttachedError`, because that design is final. An item
whose uploaded file has a submitted page mapping fails with
`UploadMappingSubmittedError`, because that file prints.

Present every candidate to the user as a numbered markdown link to its
thumbnail (and `design_url`) so they SEE each option — never only the text
summary — and use those URLs EXACTLY as returned (never build or guess one).
Number them in the order returned: the user may reply by position ("design
nr 2"), so map that number back to `candidates[n-1].design_id` yourself.
A candidate with `thumbnails_pending: true` has no preview yet: its image is
still rendering, and it may not become available. Still offer it and link its
`design_url`. Tell the user that the preview is still rendering and may not be
available, and that they can choose the design or open it in the editor anyway.
Do not say that the preview will appear.
Then let the USER choose and call `design_pick_candidate` with their chosen
`design_id` before any `design_chat`; the unpicked candidates are dropped.
While a batch is unpicked, a new call fails with `CandidatePendingError`.
If the customer rejected every candidate, offer a new batch. Call again with
`discard_unpicked=true` only after they say yes: it drops the unpicked batch.
Each order item gets at most 3 batches (`CandidateBatchLimitError`).

Returns a job — poll with poll_job until SUCCEEDED.
name: design_generate_candidates

anyOf.description:
The Runner's response to a `@runner.job` invocation.

On the fast path (work completed within budget), `status` is SUCCEEDED
or FAILED and `result` / `error` is populated. On the slow path,
`status` is RUNNING and `job_id` is the handle the host LLM uses for
`poll()`.

On FAILED, `error` is the safe class-name code; `reason` / `detail` are
populated only when the failure carries a host-safe explanation (e.g. a
RendReal rejection's server message + body), else they stay None.

On RUNNING, `note` carries model-facing guidance: it tells the host LLM whether
a widget is already polling the job, or whether it must call `poll_job` itself.

Canonical short-circuit response shape.

`status` is always `"error"` — acts as a discriminator for LLM consumers.
`error` is a machine-readable code (e.g. `session_not_found`).
`reason` is a human-readable explanation of why the call failed.
`detail` carries structured extra context (ids, available values, etc.).

title: Generate design candidates
